column1: # Measured --kv-cache-memory pins, one row per (hardware, batch shape).
# serve-mxfp4.sh consults this table automatically. A signature that is not listed falls back
# to vLLM's own memory profiling, which is always safe -- it just leaves the margin below on
# the table. ./calibrate-kv.sh measures a row for your host and writes it to
# ~/.cache/radiance-mxfp4/kv-profiles.local.tsv, which is read after this file and wins.
# WHY THESE ARE NOT COMPUTED
# vLLM sizes KV as requested_memory - non_kv_cache_memory - cudagraph_estimate, and
# non_kv_cache_memory is the profile run's TRANSIENT peak, not the steady-state need. The
# difference is real headroom, but its size depends on the activation peak at CHUNK, on the
# cudagraph capture set, and on the allocator's fragmentation on that specific card. It is
# found by pushing the pin up until startup fails and backing off, which is what
# calibrate-kv.sh automates. Do not hand-edit these toward bigger numbers: the failure mode is
# an OOM several minutes into startup, during cudagraph capture, with a traceback that blames
# whatever allocation happened to be next.
# A row is only valid for the batch shape it was measured at. MAXSEQS changes the cudagraph
# capture sizes and the activation peak; CHUNK changes the prefill transient directly.
# sig                 maxseqs chunk   maxlen  spec    bytes           note

column7: 2x R9700 32 GiB, gfx1201; 943,581 KV tokens vs 892,799 profiled (+5.7%); survives a full 260k prefill sweep

1x R9700 32 GiB, gfx1201, TP=1 single-GPU profile; measured 2026-09-16 on the NVFP4 checkpoint (the largest footprint served: bf16 lm_head) from a pinned start (its profile run cannot reach the minimum); 7.00 GiB served 161,057 tokens, 7.60 OOM, backed off one step; ~140k KV tokens at the pin

1x R9700 32 GiB, gfx1201, TP=1 long-context shape; ~220k KV tokens. REPORTED by a user at these settings, NOT measured here by calibrate-kv.sh -- unlike every other row in this file. Consistent with the 65536 row's 40.6 KB/token (9.13 GB / 40.6 KB = 225k), and the smaller batch (seqs 8->3, chunk 4096->2560) genuinely frees the extra memory, so it is a new key rather than an inflated one. Re-measure with calibrate-kv.sh before trusting it on other hardware.
